name: Highlands

facts.text: Highlands' Tree Management Bylaw No. 10 (1994) needs a tree cutting permit to remove a protected tree or any tree near a watercourse, lake or steep slope, and prohibits cutting a significant tree.
facts.excerpt: cutting down a significant tree is strictly prohibited
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: The District lists Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood, Pacific yew, cascara and manzanita as protected trees.
facts.excerpt: Under the Tree Management Bylaw protected trees are:

facts.text: Building or subdividing inside Highlands' Steep Slopes, Water and Riparian, or Sensitive Vegetation development permit areas needs a development permit first; what is on the ground decides whether a lot is in one.
facts.sourceTitle: Development Permit Areas 1-5 (District of Highlands, Jan 2024)
facts.excerpt: DP Area #1 - Steep Slopes, DP Area #2 - Water and Riparian Areas, DP Area #3 - Sensitive Vegetation

facts.text: Most Highlands homes draw drinking water from private wells in a bedrock aquifer (BC Aquifer #680), so irrigation is planned around well yield. CRD watering rules apply only to the few connected properties.
facts.sourceTitle: Groundwater Protection - Final Work Plan and Implementation Report (District of Highlands)
facts.excerpt: the majority of residents in the District obtain their drinking water from private wells that tap into the local bedrock aquifer
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: Many Highlands wells are high in iron, which can stain paving, siding and plants watered by sprinklers; the District advises testing tap water at least yearly.
facts.excerpt: many wells in the Highlands are high in iron
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Staining is our inference, not a District statement; which Highlands page holds the iron sentence was unclear in the snippet.

facts.text: Highlands has no open burning season: a free permit is required for every open burn, all year, and fires larger than a campfire are allowed only when the venting index is 'Good'.
facts.excerpt: permits are mandatory year-round and are free of charge
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. One page cites Bylaw No. 264, another the Fire Control and Protection Bylaw No. 474, 2025; confirm the current bylaw.

facts.text: Highlands homes sit among forest at the wildland-urban interface. The District has a Community Wildfire Protection Plan (2009) and offers free FireSmart home assessments, which often lead to fuel reduction around buildings.
facts.excerpt: a free home assessment with no obligation
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. CWPP: https://www.highlands.ca/sites/31/files/2025-02/Highlands_CWPP%20-%20r.pdf (Blackwell, Dec 2009).

facts.text: Groundwater in Highlands also serves the Hanington Estates subdivision, and Bear Mountain Golf Course irrigation draws on Highlands wells.
facts.sourceTitle: 2018 Groundwater Level Monitoring Report (District of Highlands)
facts.excerpt: Hanington Estates subdivision is served by groundwater wells
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. From the 2018 report; may have changed.

facts.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm. Most Highlands homes are on private wells and only some areas are connected, so check before applying it.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Dates and day split also shown in the Saanich watering-schedules page snippet. Shared regional block, not municipality-specific.

facts.text: B.C.'s Wildlife Act (section 34) protects occupied bird nests, and eagle, osprey, heron and some other nests year-round, so trees are checked for active nests before felling or heavy pruning, especially in spring and summer.
facts.sourceTitle: Wildlife - Environmental regulatory compliance (Province of B.C.)
facts.excerpt: The protection for eagle and heron nests applies even outside of the breeding season.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Provincial rule: shared regional block.
